drivingQuestion: How can one dig with an embedded shovel without crushing or making a hole?
outcomeNote: Loose earth avoids crushing; the hole is exempt per R' Abba.

segments.en: Here it is referring «to loose earth» that does not require further crushing.

segments.he: וְהָא קָא עָבֵיד גּוּמָּא! כִּדְרַבִּי אַבָּא. דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: הַחוֹפֵר גּוּמָּא בְּשַׁבָּת, וְאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ אֶלָּא לַעֲפָרָהּ — פָּטוּר עָלֶיהָ.
segments.en: The Gemara challenges this: «But» even in the case of loose earth, «one makes a hole» by the very act of removing the earth or the shovel from that place. The Gemara answers: This ruling is «in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Abba, as Rabbi Abba said: One who digs a hole on Shabbat,» but he «needs only its earth» and has no interest in forming a pit, «is exempt for» that act. Since he has no interest in the hole, he is considered to have performed a destructive act, and the halakha is that one who commits a destructive act is not liable for the performance of prohibited labor on Shabbat and Festivals.
